title: Nine times narrower at the node boundary
caption: The per-direction budget on each side of the node edge: 8 GPUs at 450 GB/s each inside the NVLink domain, a 50 GB/s NDR port at the first hop off the node. The ~9x cliff has persisted since NVLink's first product year in 2016; placement, deciding what may cross, is the design response.

title: Two regimes, one line
caption: Message time T(n) = alpha + n/beta on log axes: the alpha floor rules below the crossover (75 KB on NDR), the beta slope rules above. The 4 KB control message lives on the flat part at 1.58 us; the 350 MB shard lives on the slope at 7.0 ms. Doubling beta halves the slope and leaves the floor untouched.

title: Oversubscription prices the cut
caption: A two-tier fat-tree at radix 64 reaching 2,048 hosts at 1:1 (bisection 25.6 TB/s) versus the same leaves oversubscribed 4:1 (6.4 TB/s). Worst-case ring AllReduce crossing the cut: 0.20 s vs 0.80 s. The 2:1 middle still costs 23.1% of throughput and, on the book's \$300M cluster, the 4:1 choice burns ~\$142.1M.

title: 256 senders, one port, five microseconds
caption: One SuperPOD scalable unit worth of senders converging on a single 50 GB/s egress: 12.8 TB/s offered, a 32 MB buffer that nominally holds 640 us of backlog, overflow in under 5 us. The bandwidth-delay product at a 5 us feedback RTT is only 250 KB, so reaction always arrives late; scheduling, not buffering, is the fix.
